items.title: Basis for entry checks and editorial preparation suggestions

values: Materials and settings｜all editorial fictional paper-and-pencil exercises

You are the work order checker at a fictional printing plant and need to make a first-article and spot-check card for 1,200 A4 double-sided four-color flyers; do not touch machines and do not fill in directly executable setting values.

A1: the work order reads A4, 1,200 conforming copies, double-sided four-color, 120 gsm paper; check the ink color and registration of the approved proof. Trial-run losses and the actual number of sheets fed are unknown.
A2: the editors set one sheet out of every 200 for sampling, with sample numbers 1, 201, 401, 601, 801, and 1001; the sampling plan is for practice only and does not represent a plant standard.
Task and output

A3: samples 1, 801, and 1001 conform; 201 has registration misalignment, 401 is too light in cyan, and 601 has ink scuffing. A4: the batch has not been released and the other 1,194 sheets were not observed.

A5: the practitioner only records and proposes isolation; the quality inspection responsible person decides on release or rework, and only trained operators may set machines under on-site procedure. Submit the calculation, the sampling defect table, the items still to be verified, and the escalation target.
Reference approach (do it independently first)

A5: 1,200 double-sided sheets make 2,400 printed sides, which is the number of sides in the finished product and does not equal the number of machine sheet passes or the ink consumption. 3 of the 6 sample sheets have defects, which is only a 50% sample share.

List the different defects in 201, 401, and 601; suspend the affected batch and hand the scope to the quality responsible person for judgment, and machine adjustment is performed by authorized personnel.

Others should be able to recalculate 2,400 printed sides from A1–A5 and find the six sample sheets, the three defect types, and the 1,194 unobserved sheets.

description.text: Printing press operators set up digital, offset, or flexographic equipment against the work order, check paper, ink, and plates, and pull trial proofs to check ink color, density, and registration; during the batch they spot-check, record defects, and escalate anomalies. See the United States 51-5112 wage and employment data, the Chinese wage evidence boundaries, work risks, entry exercises, and career paths.

subject.name: Printing press operators
subject.summary: Printing press operators read production work orders, check paper and ink, and set plate, ink feed, registration, and sheet feed parameters; they start the press and pull a trial proof, check ink color, density, and registration position, and keep spot-checking and recording anomalies during the production run. On jams, unusual noises, or guard failure, they stop the press according to on-site procedure and hand it to authorized personnel.
